units.text: INT. WOMAN - CONTINUOUS
To Doctor Daubeny.
You see I have got Mrs. Arbuthnot to come to me at last.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: That is a great honour, Lady Hunstanton. Mrs. Daubeny will be quite jealous of you.
units.name: THE ARCHDEACON

units.text: Ah, I am so sorry Mrs. Daubeny could not come with you to-night. Headache as usual, I suppose.
units.name: LADY HUNSTANTON

units.text: Yes, Lady Hunstanton; a perfect martyr. But she is happiest alone. She is happiest alone.
units.name: THE ARCHDEACON

units.text: To her husband .
John!
units.name: LADY CAROLINE

units.text: SIR JOHN goes over to his wife .
Doctor Daubeny talks to LADY HUNSTANTON and MRS. ARBUTHNOT.
MRS. ARBUTHNOT watches LORD ILLINGWORTH the whole time.
He has passed across the room without noticing her, and approaches MRS. ALLONBY, who with LADY STUTFIELD is standing by the door looking on to the terrace.
How is the most charming woman in the world?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Taking LADY STUTFIELD by the hand.
We are both quite well, thank you, Lord Illingworth. But what a short time you have been in the dining-room! It seems as if we had only just left.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I was bored to death. Never opened my lips the whole time. Absolutely longing to come in to you.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: You should have. The American girl has been giving us a lecture.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: Really? All Americans lecture, I believe. I suppose it is something in their climate. What did she lecture about?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Oh, Puritanism, of course.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: I am going to convert her, am I not? How long do you give me?
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: A week.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: A week is more than enough.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Enter GERALD and LORD ALFRED.
Going to MRS. ARBUTHNOT.
Dear mother!
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Gerald, I don’t feel at all well. See me home, Gerald. I shouldn’t have come.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: I am so sorry, mother. Certainly. But you must know Lord Illingworth first.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Goes across room .
Not to-night, Gerald.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Lord Illingworth, I want you so much to know my mother.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: With the greatest pleasure.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: To MRS. ALLONBY.
I’ll be back in a moment. People’s mothers always bore me to death. All women become like their mothers. That is their tragedy.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: No man does. That is his.
units.name: MRS. ALLONBY

units.text: What a delightful mood you are in to-night!
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: Turns round and goes across with GERALD to MRS. ARBUTHNOT.
When he sees her , he starts back in wonder .
Then slowly his eyes turn towards GERALD.
Mother, this is Lord Illingworth, who has offered to take me as his private secretary.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: MRS. ARBUTHNOT bows coldly .
It is a wonderful opening for me, isn’t it? I hope he won’t be disappointed in me, that is all. You’ll thank Lord Illingworth, mother, won’t you?
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Lord Illingworth is very good, I am sure, to interest himself in you for the moment.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Putting his hand on GERALD’S shoulder .
Oh, Gerald and I are great friends already, Mrs . . . Arbuthnot.
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: There can be nothing in common between you and my son, Lord Illingworth.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Dear mother, how can you say so? Of course Lord Illingworth is awfully clever and that sort of thing. There is nothing Lord Illingworth doesn’t know.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: My dear boy!
units.name: LORD ILLINGWORTH

units.text: He knows more about life than any one I have ever met. I feel an awful duffer when I am with you, Lord Illingworth. Of course, I have had so few advantages. I have not been to Eton or Oxford like other chaps. But Lord Illingworth doesn’t seem to mind that. He has been awfully good to me, mother.
units.name: GERALD

units.text: Lord Illingworth may change his mind. He may not really want you as his secretary.
units.name: MRS. ARBUTHNOT

units.text: Mother!
units.name: GERALD
